review_notes:
I read the whole file and checked the definitions it introduces: threeProfilePoint, threeProfileCenter, threeEnvelopeExponent, threeNormalEquiv, threeNormalMetric, threeCouplingRadius, threeGlobalRadius, threeGlobalLog, threeNormalInv, threeNormalGlue, threeNormalMetricOf and ThreeCleanBall. I also grepped the project for the supporting types and definitions: ThreeModel, ThreeManifold, NormalWaveSpace, linearPullbackMetric, manifoldChartPush, IsSmoothNeighborhood and CoordinateForm. All of these are bespoke objects tied to the sphere-metric construction. The exceptions are threeNormalEquiv, which already builds on Mathlib's ContinuousLinearEquiv.ofFinrankEq, and threeProfilePoint, which is an explicit point of Sphere 2. None reimplements a Mathlib concept. The repeated `local instance ... := inferInstance` declarations only restore instances locally and do not introduce a competing concept.

The one overlap I saw is internal to the project, not with Mathlib. threeNormalMetric (line 187) is threeNormalMetricOf (line ~610) applied to threeBackgroundMetric, up to unfolding. The first is the specialisation and the second the parametrised family, and the specialised name is used 25 times in this file's group of files, so I did not treat it as a defect under this rubric. The near-duplicate proofs of the global profile family theorems are theorem or proof duplication, which the rubric excludes. I have no remaining uncertainty beyond not having compiled any replacement.
